newsitem.title: LITHUANIA: Lithuanian shares ease in dull trade.
newsitem.headline: Lithuanian shares ease in dull trade.

text.p: Lithuanian shares eased on Friday in dull trade as foreign investors were sidelined by the Good Friday holiday.
The Litin A index slid 31.17 points to 2,606.97 and overall central market volume was only 715,000 litas.
Dealers said demand was low as Lithuania was of the few European markets open and foreign investors stayed away.
Buyers are also digesting the results of a spate of shareholders' meetings this week.
Dealers said they expected shares to continue easing next week.
"They (shares) seem to have hit their peak for the time being," said Arvydas Jacikevicius of brokerage firm Suprema.
The session's losers included tractor parts producer Kuro aparatura, which fell to 11.73 litas from 12.10 litas in trade of 11,500 litas.
The Lithuania Sea Shipping Company also eased, with its price dipping to 8.31 litas from 8.90 litas in trade worth 120,000 litas.

The huge state-run Savings Bank, which reported a 1996 net profit of 30 million litas after a loss of 30 million litas the previous year, saw its share price drop to 270.00 litas from 276.00 litas in trade of close to 25,000 litas.
The bank announced on Friday that it would pay a dividend of 2.8 million litas and use the rest of its profit to cover 1995's big losses.
Block trades amounted to over 660,000 litas.
